title: unify-terraform-private-state-layout-and-refactor-gpu-node-pools-iam-networking
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: our private deployment terraform modules have diverged across installs (GKE, EKS, on-prem) and the GPU node pool, IAM, and networking modules have islanded state layouts which complicates upgrades and cross-account permissions. This PR unifies the state layout and refactors the GPU node pool module to be reusable across cloud providers, extracts least-privilege IAM role templates, and updates VPC/networking wiring to support shared subnets for private deployments.

What this PR does: - Introduces a new unified state layout under modules/state that separates immutable infra (vpc, network) from mutable nodepool data so upgrades don't require replacing state. - Refactors modules/gpu_node_pool to support a provider-agnostic input schema (instance_type/node_taints/autoscaling) and splits bootstrap scripts into templates/ so customer on-prem use-cases can override init flows. - Adds modules/iam/roles.tf with a minimal private-control-plane role and node-pool agent role, and documents required trust relationships. - Updates modules/networking to support shared-subnet attachment and cross-project routes; makes static IP allocation optional for control-plane endpoints. - Adds a migration script scripts/migrations/2026-02-unify-state.sh that helps move existing Terraform state to the new layout (copy+mv dance with state locking). - Adds tests/terraform/plan-output.txt and a smoke test in CI to validate plan diffs for a sample private deployment.

Checklist: - [x] Module refactor completed and unit-tested locally - [x] Migration script added and tested against a staging workspace - [x] Documentation updated with upgrade and rollback guidance - [x] CI plan/format checks passing

Why: This reduces engineer friction during upgrades, enables safer rollouts of GPU autoscaling changes, and enforces least-privilege for private control plane components.

Migration notes: The included migration script must be run from a machine with access to the existing state backend. It will create a backup workspace, perform state mv operations for previously-namespaced resources, and validate with terraform plan. See migration_notes field for step-by-step instructions.

Rollout: we will first merge to main behind a feature flag; we will run the migration for one private customer in staging, confirm no delta in resource replacement, then run for remaining customers in a maintenance window.

migration_notes: Run scripts/migrations/2026-02-unify-state.sh --dry-run against your staging workspace first. Steps: 1) Ensure backend access and terraform v1.4+. 2) Take a backend snapshot (terraform state pull > backup.json). 3) Run the script in --dry-run to audit planned state mv operations. 4) Create a new workspace (e.g., staging-unified) and run the script without --dry-run to perform state mv. 5) Run terraform plan against the new workspace and validate that no resources are scheduled for replacement. 6) If plan looks good, repeat for production during maintenance window. The script will create a backup workspace prefixed with backup-<timestamp> before mutating state.
testing_plan: Local: unit tests for role policy generation, terraform init+plan against examples with mocked backend. CI: added ci/terraform-plan-private.yml which spins up an ephemeral backend, runs terraform init and plan, and compares plan to tests/terraform/plan-output.txt. Manual: run migration script in staging and validate no replacement.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature-flag and wait for CI to validate examples. 2) Run migration in staging for one customer and validate metrics (no node replacements, control-plane stable). 3) Run incremental migrations for remaining customers during maintenance windows. 4) After all customers migrated, remove compatibility shim in 2 weeks.
rollback_instructions: If migration causes unexpected resource replacements: 1) Pause further migrations. 2) Use terraform workspace to switch to the backup workspace created by the migration script (backup-<timestamp>). 3) Run 'terraform apply' on the backup workspace to ensure state is restored. 4) Revert to the previous module version using the rollback branch and apply in the same workspace. 5) Open an incident and follow cutover playbook if nodes are impacted.
notes_for_sre: The new networking changes add optional shared_subnet boolean; set to true for setups that rely on centralized VPCs. For GKE deployments ensure private cluster master authorized networks are updated before rolling. Monitor node replacement telemetry and PV attachment latencies during migration.
